title: PADO-Pauli: A GPU-Accelerated Implementation of Pauli Propagation
abstract: Variational quantum algorithms utilize parameterized circuits many times during training, at new parameter values, over batches of data, and with gradients. Pauli propagation approximates the expectation values of such circuits classically by evolving the observable in the Heisenberg picture as a truncated sum of Pauli strings. We present PADO-Pauli, a GPU engine for Pauli propagation that compiles a circuit and its observables once into sparse matrices in which each rotation angle contributes only a cosine and a sine factor, so every later evaluation reuses the compiled program. It evaluates batches of parameters and data inputs embedded as rotation angles. By default its gradients come from a vector-Jacobian product registered with PyTorch's automatic differentiation, so they flow through the angles to any classical layer that produces them. PADO-Pauli also provides truncation by Pauli weight and coefficient size, and noise channels. Zero-filtering removes terms that do not contribute to an expectation value in the all-zero reference state and makes the batched forward pass about 1.5 times faster. Compared to cuPauliProp on an NVIDIA A100, PADO-Pauli evaluates up to 10 times faster on 4 to 12 qubits and uses up to 3.1 times less memory on 16 qubits. We check its accuracy against exact statevector simulation up to 28 qubits. These features make PADO-Pauli a practical toolkit for training variational quantum algorithms, including quantum machine learning models.
summary: This paper introduces PADO-Pauli, a highly optimized, GPU-accelerated toolkit for performing Pauli propagation—the classical evaluation of quantum circuit expectation values. By compiling circuits once and reusing the structure for batched evaluations with automatic differentiation, it drastically speeds up the training of variational quantum algorithms. This makes complex quantum simulations practical for modern quantum machine learning research.
main_problem: The paper addresses the need for an efficient classical method to evaluate expectation values of parameterized quantum circuits, which are central to training variational quantum algorithms (VQAs).
main_result: PADO-Pauli is presented as a GPU-accelerated engine that significantly outperforms existing tools, achieving up to 10x speedup and lower memory usage compared to competitors.
method: It uses Pauli propagation in the Heisenberg picture, compiling the circuit and observables into sparse matrices that are reused for multiple evaluations, including native gradient calculation via PyTorch's automatic differentiation.
model_or_system: The system involves parameterized quantum circuits whose observables are represented as sums of Pauli strings. The method approximates the expectation value by evolving the observable through the circuit gates.
key_observables: Expectation values of Pauli strings, Pauli weight, and coefficient size.
important_parameters: Number of qubits (up to 28 checked), rotation angles ($	heta$), Pauli weight truncation limit ($w_{	ext{max}}$), and coefficient size threshold ($\epsilon$).
main_assumptions: The method relies on truncation (by Pauli weight and coefficient size) to keep the computation tractable, and the total error is bounded by the sum of discarded coefficient masses.
figures_summary: Figure 1 provides an overview of the PADO-Pauli workflow, illustrating single compilation, step-wise truncation, and subsequent multiple evaluations with gradient tracking.
paper_structure: The paper details the theoretical basis of Pauli propagation, introduces the PADO-Pauli GPU engine for compilation and evaluation, discusses various truncation and noise modeling techniques, and concludes with performance comparisons against state-of-the-art tools.
why_interesting: This work provides a crucial, high-performance computational backend for implementing and training quantum machine learning models, which is vital for any theoretical physicist working on quantum algorithms.
